pairs: Et factum est cum intraret Jesus in domum cujusdam principis pharisæorum sabbato manducare panem,
And it happened that, when Jesus entered the house of a certain leader of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread,
Et ecce homo quidam hydropicus erat ante illum.
And behold, a certain man before him was afflicted with edema.
Et respondens Jesus dixit ad legisperitos
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law and to the Pharisees,
“Is it lawful to cure on the Sabbath?”
But they kept silent. Yet truly,
Ipse vero apprehensum sanavit eum, ac dimisit.
taking hold of him, he healed him and sent him away.
And responding to them, he said,
Cujus vestrum asinus, aut bos in puteum cadet,
“Which of you will have a donkey or an ox fall into a pit,
et non continuo extrahet illum die sabbati?
and will not promptly pull him out, on the day of the Sabbath?”
Et non poterant ad hæc respondere illi.
And they were unable to respond to him about these things.
Then he also told a parable,
noticing how they chose the first seats at the table,
“When you are invited to a wedding,
do not sit down in the first place,
ne forte honoratior te sit invitatus ab illo.
lest perhaps someone more honored than yourself may have been invited by him.
Et veniens is, qui te et illum vocavit,
And then he who called both you and him, approaching,
et tunc incipias cum rubore novissimum locum tenere.
And then you would begin, with shame, to take the last place.
sit down in the lowest place,
when he who invited you arrives,
Tunc erit tibi gloria coram simul discumbentibus:
Then you will have glory in the sight of those who sit at table together with you.
quia omnis, qui se exaltat, humiliabitur:
For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled,
and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.”
Dicebat autem et ei, qui invitaverat:
Then he also said to the one who had invited him:
“When you prepare a lunch or dinner,
noli vocare amicos tuos, neque fratres tuos,
do not choose to call your friends, or your brothers,
ne forte te et ipsi reinvitent, et fiat tibi retributio;
lest perhaps they might then invite you in return and repayment would made to you.
But when you prepare a feast,
And you will be blessed because they do not have a way to repay you.
retribuetur enim tibi in resurrectione justorum.
your recompense will be in the resurrection of the just.”
Hæc cum audisset quidam de simul discumbentibus,
When someone sitting at table with him had heard these things,
Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno Dei.
“Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of God.”
“A certain man prepared a great feast,
Et misit servum suum hora cœnæ dicere invitatis ut venirent,
And he sent his servant, at the hour of the feast, to tell the invited to come;
Et cœperunt simul omnes excusare. Primus dixit ei:
And at once they all began to make excuses.
Villam emi, et necesse habeo exire,
The first said to him: ‘I bought a farm,
and I need to go out and see it.
I ask you to excuse me.’
et eo probare illa: rogo te,
and I am going to examine them.
I ask you to excuse me.’
and therefore I am not able to go.’
Et reversus servus nuntiavit hæc domino suo.
And returning, the servant reported these things to his lord.
Then the father of the family, becoming angry,
Exi cito in plateas et vicos civitatis:
‘Go out quickly into the streets and neighborhoods of the city.
and the blind, and the lame.’
‘It has been done, just as you ordered,
lord, and there is still room.’
And the lord said to the servant:
so that my house may be filled.
Dico autem vobis quod nemo virorum illorum qui vocati sunt,
that none of those men who were invited will taste of my feast.’”
Ibant autem turbæ multæ cum eo:
Now great crowds traveled with him.
And turning around, he said to them:
and does not hate his father,
he is not able to be my disciple.
Et qui non bajulat crucem suam,
And whoever does not bear his cross
is not able to be my disciple.
Quis enim ex vobis volens turrim ædificare,
would not first sit down and determine the costs that are required,
to see if he has the means to complete it?
posteaquam posuerit fundamentum, et non potuerit perficere,
after he will have laid the foundation and not been able to finish it,
omnes qui vident, incipiant illudere ei,
everyone who sees it may begin to mock him,
Quia hic homo cœpit ædificare, et non potuit consummare?
‘This man began to build what he was not able to finish.’
Aut quis rex iturus committere bellum adversus alium regem,
Or, what king, advancing to engage in war against another king,
non sedens prius cogitat, si possit cum decem millibus occurrere ei,
would not first sit down and consider whether he may be able, with ten thousand,
qui cum viginti millibus venit ad se?
to meet one who comes against him with twenty thousand?
If not, then while the other is still far away,
legationem mittens rogat ea quæ pacis sunt.
sending a delegation, he would ask him for terms of peace.
Sic ergo omnis ex vobis, qui non renuntiat omnibus quæ possidet, non potest meus esse discipulus.
Therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses is not able to be my disciple.
But if the salt has lost its flavor,
with what will it be seasoned?
It is useful neither in soil,
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
